reliability: Public vendor page read directly with curl; HTTP 200. Primary evidence of advertised scope only, not independently tested functionality or customer demand.
findings: The page describes a construction payroll service: contractors submit timecards, and payroll experts handle payroll; it claims integration with QuickBooks accounting data.

Listed capabilities include multiple jobs/trades/pay rates on a timecard, automated pay rates/fringes by employee/job/trade, and print/electronic certified payroll reports for LCPtracker, eMars, DIR and more.
The vendor says reports are generated after each payroll and can be downloaded after the pay period.
limitations: This is a managed-payroll alternative rather than proof that an add-on export works with every existing payroll stack.
The precise QuickBooks integration scope, input conversion, current versions, fees and switching costs were not verified.
Selected vendor testimonials and unsourced competitor assertions are not treated as independent market evidence.
No independent small-contractor time/cost measurement, failure rate or willingness-to-pay evidence.
title: Payroll4Construction for QuickBooks Desktop Users
